sanskrit: yadā tv asaṃgṛhītatvāt prayānty aśvā yathāsukham tato duḥśāsanaḥ sūtaṃ buddhavān gatacetasam
english: But when the horses, no longer held in check, ran on at their own pleasure, then Duḥśāsana realized that his charioteer had lost his senses.

sanskrit: sa hayān saṃnigṛhyājau svayaṃ hayaviśāradaḥ yuyudhe rathināṃ śreṣṭhaś citraṃ laghu ca suṣṭhu ca
english: Skilled himself in handling horses, he reined them in upon the field and, foremost of chariot-warriors, fought on with a craft at once dazzling, swift, and sure.

sanskrit: tad asyāpūjayan karma sve pare caiva saṃyuge hatasūtarathenājau vyacarad yad abhītavat
english: Both his own men and his foes in that battle honored this feat of his—that with charioteer slain he ranged across the field as one without fear.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu tān aśvāṃs tīkṣṇair bāṇair avākirat pīḍyamānāḥ śaraiś cāśu prādravaṃs te tatas tataḥ
english: But Sahadeva covered those horses with his sharp arrows, and tormented by the shafts they at once bolted this way and that.

sanskrit: sa raśmiṣu viṣaktatvād utsasarja śarāsanam dhanuṣā karma kurvaṃs tu raśmīn sa punar utsṛjat
english: Since the reins entangled him, he let go his bow; and when he plied his bow in action, he again let go the reins.

sanskrit: chidreṣu teṣu taṃ bāṇair mādrīputro 'bhyavākirat parīpsaṃs tvatsutaṃ karṇas tadantaram avāpatat
english: In those openings the son of Mādrī covered him with arrows; but Karṇa, seeking to save your son, swooped into the breach.

sanskrit: vṛkodaras tataḥ karṇaṃ tribhir bhallaiḥ samāhitaiḥ ākarṇapūrṇair abhyaghnan bāhvor urasi cānadat
english: Then Vṛkodara struck Karṇa with three well-aimed broad-headed shafts, drawn back to the ear, upon both arms and on the chest, and roared aloud.

sanskrit: saṃnyavartata taṃ karṇaḥ saṃghaṭṭita ivoragaḥ tad abhūt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ bhīmarādheyayos tadā
english: Karṇa turned upon him like a serpent that has been trodden on, and then there arose a tumultuous battle between Bhīma and the son of Rādhā.

sanskrit: tau vṛṣāv iva saṃkruddhau vivṛttanayanāv ubhau vegena mahatānyonyaṃ saṃrabdhāv abhipetatuḥ
english: Like two enraged bulls, both with eyes rolling, the two in fury fell upon each other with tremendous speed.

sanskrit: abhisaṃśliṣṭayos tatra tayor āhavaśauṇḍayoḥ abhinnaśarapātatvād gadāyuddham avartata
english: As those two passionate warriors closed and locked together, and the fall of their arrows could no longer divide them, the fight turned to a duel of maces.

sanskrit: gadayā bhīmasenas tu karṇasya rathakūbaram bibhedāśu tadā rājaṃs tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: With his mace Bhīmasena at once shattered the pole of Karṇa's chariot, O king, and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tato bhīmasya rādheyo gadām ādāya vīryavān avāsṛjad rathe tāṃ tu bibheda gadayā gadām
english: Then the valiant son of Rādhā took up a mace and hurled it at Bhīma's chariot; but Bhīma with his own mace broke that mace asunder.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaḥ punar gurvīṃ cikṣepādhirather gadām tāṃ śarair daśabhiḥ karṇaḥ supuṅkhaiḥ susamāhitaiḥ pratyavidhyat punaś cānyaiḥ sā bhīmaṃ punar āvrajat
english: Then Bhīma again flung a heavy mace at the charioteer; but Karṇa struck it back with ten well-feathered, well-aimed shafts, and then with others, so that it returned once more toward Bhīma.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pratinipātena bhīmasya vipulo dhvajaḥ papāta sārathiś cāsya mumoha gadayā hataḥ
english: By the recoiling fall of that mace Bhīma's tall banner came down, and his charioteer, struck by it, swooned away.

sanskrit: sa karṇe sāyakān aṣṭau vyasṛjat krodhamūrchitaḥ dhvaje śarāsane caiva śarāvāpe ca bhārata
english: Maddened with wrath, he loosed eight arrows at Karṇa—at his banner, his bow, and his quiver, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ punas tu rādheyo hayān asya ratheṣubhiḥ ṛṣyavarṇāñ jaghānāśu tathobhau pārṣṇisārathī
english: Then again the son of Rādhā with chariot-shafts swiftly slew his antelope-colored horses, and both his flank-guarding drivers as well.

sanskrit: sa vipannaratho bhīmo nakulasyāpluto ratham harir yathā gireḥ śṛṅgaṃ samākrāmad ariṃdamaḥ
english: His chariot disabled, Bhīma the foe-subduer leapt onto Nakula's car, as a lion springs to a mountain peak.

sanskrit: tathā droṇārjunau citram ayudhyetāṃ mahārathau ācāryaśiṣyau rājendra kṛtapraharaṇau yudhi
english: Meanwhile Droṇa and Arjuna, those great chariot-warriors, teacher and pupil, both masters of striking in battle, fought on wondrously, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: laghusaṃdhānayogābhyāṃ rathayoś ca raṇena ca mohayantau manuṣyāṇāṃ cakṣūṃṣi ca manāṃsi ca
english: With swift nocking of arrows and with the wheeling combat of their two cars, they bewildered both the eyes and the minds of men.

sanskrit: upāramanta te sarve yodhāsmākaṃ pare tathā adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ paśyantas tad yuddhaṃ guruśiṣyayoḥ
english: Our warriors and the foes alike all paused, beholding that never-before-seen combat of teacher and pupil.

sanskrit: vicitrān pṛtanāmadhye rathamārgān udīryataḥ anyonyam apasavyaṃ ca kartuṃ vīrau tadaiṣatuḥ parākramaṃ tayor yodhā dadṛśus taṃ suvismitāḥ
english: As they drove their cars in wondrous, ever-shifting courses through the midst of the army, each hero sought to keep the other on his right; and the warriors gazed upon their prowess, filled with amazement.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ droṇapāṇḍavayor mahat āmiṣārthaṃ mahārāja gagane śyenayor iva
english: Mighty was the battle that arose between those two, Droṇa and the son of Pāṇḍu, O great king, like that of two hawks in the sky contending for a piece of flesh.

sanskrit: yad yac cakāra droṇas tu kuntīputrajigīṣayā tat tat pratijaghānāśu prahasaṃs tasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Whatever Droṇa attempted in his desire to defeat the son of Kuntī, all of it the Pāṇḍava at once countered, laughing the while.

sanskrit: yadā droṇo na śaknoti pāṇḍavasya viśeṣaṇe tataḥ prāduścakārāstram astramārgaviśāradaḥ
english: When Droṇa found he could not gain the upper hand over the Pāṇḍava, then, skilled in the ways of celestial weapons, he brought forth his missiles.

sanskrit: aindraṃ pāśupataṃ tvāṣṭraṃ vāyavyam atha vāruṇam muktaṃ muktaṃ droṇacāpāt taj jaghāna dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: The weapons of Indra, of Paśupati, of Tvaṣṭṛ, of Vāyu, and of Varuṇa—each as it sped from Droṇa's bow, Dhanaṃjaya struck down.

sanskrit: astrāṇy astrair yadā tasya vidhivad dhanti pāṇḍavaḥ tato 'straiḥ paramair divyair droṇaḥ pārtham avākirat
english: When the Pāṇḍava duly quelled his weapons with weapons, Droṇa then overwhelmed Pārtha with the highest celestial missiles.

sanskrit: yad yad astraṃ sa pārthāya prayuṅkte vijigīṣayā tasyāstrasya vighātārthaṃ tat tat sa kurute 'rjunaḥ
english: Whatever weapon he loosed at Pārtha in his will to conquer, Arjuna fashioned the very means to undo that weapon.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamāneṣv astreṣu divyeṣv api yathāvidhi arjunenārjunaṃ droṇo manasaivābhyapūjayat
english: As Arjuna duly quelled even his celestial weapons, Droṇa honored Arjuna within his very heart.

sanskrit: mene cātmānam adhikaṃ pṛthivyām api bhārata tena śiṣyeṇa sarvebhyaḥ śastravidbhyaḥ samantataḥ
english: And he reckoned himself, O Bhārata, exalted upon the earth above all who know the use of arms, by reason of such a pupil.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇas tu pārthena tathā madhye mahātmanām yatamāno 'rjunaṃ prītyā pratyavārayad utsmayan
english: Held in check by Pārtha thus before the great-souled host, yet striving on, with a smile and with affection he warded Arjuna off in turn.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe devāś ca gandharvāś ca sahasraśaḥ ṛṣayaḥ siddhasaṃghāś ca vyatiṣṭhanta didṛkṣayā
english: Then in the firmament the gods and gandharvas by the thousand, the sages and the hosts of siddhas, took their stand, eager to behold.

sanskrit: tad apsarobhir ākīrṇaṃ yakṣarākṣasasaṃkulam śrīmad ākāśam abhavad bhūyo meghākulaṃ yathā
english: Thronged with apsarases and crowded with yakṣas and rākṣasas, the splendid sky grew dense as though massed with clouds.

sanskrit: tatra smāntarhitā vāco vyacaranta punaḥ punaḥ droṇasya stavasaṃyuktāḥ pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ visṛjyamāneṣv astreṣu jvālayatsu diśo daśa
english: There unseen voices passed back and forth again and again, joined in praise of Droṇa and of the great-souled Pārtha, as the weapons were loosed, setting the ten directions ablaze.

sanskrit: naivedaṃ mānuṣaṃ yuddhaṃ nāsuraṃ na ca rākṣasam na daivaṃ na ca gāndharvaṃ brāhmaṃ dhruvam idaṃ param vicitram idam āścaryaṃ na no dṛṣṭaṃ na ca śrutam
english: "This is no human combat, nor of the asuras, nor of the rākṣasas, nor of the gods, nor of the gandharvas; surely this is supreme and Brahmic. Wondrous and marvelous is this—never have we seen its like, nor heard of it."

sanskrit: ati pāṇḍavam ācāryo droṇaṃ cāpy ati pāṇḍavaḥ nānayor antaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śakyam astreṇa kena cit
english: "The teacher surpasses the Pāṇḍava, and the Pāṇḍava surpasses Droṇa; no difference between the two can be discerned by any weapon."

sanskrit: yadi rudro dvidhākṛtya yudhyetātmānam ātmanā tatra śakyopamā kartum anyatra tu na vidyate
english: "Were Rudra to divide himself in two and fight himself against himself, there a comparison might be drawn—but nowhere else is it to be found."

sanskrit: jñānam ekastham ācārye jñānaṃ yogaś ca pāṇḍave śauryam ekastham ācārye balaṃ śauryaṃ ca pāṇḍave
english: "In the teacher knowledge dwells alone; in the Pāṇḍava, knowledge and discipline both. In the teacher valor dwells alone; in the Pāṇḍava, strength and valor both."

sanskrit: nemau śakyau maheṣvāsau raṇe kṣepayituṃ paraiḥ icchamānau punar imau hanyetāṃ sāmaraṃ jagat
english: "These two great bowmen cannot be flung down in battle by their foes; and should they so will it, the two could slay the whole world together with its gods."

sanskrit: ity abruvan mahārāja dṛṣṭvā tau puruṣarṣabhau antarhitāni bhūtāni prakāśāni ca saṃghaśaḥ
english: Thus spoke, O great king, beholding those two bulls among men, the invisible beings and the visible ones, in throng upon throng.

sanskrit: tato droṇo brāhmam astraṃ prāduścakre mahāmatiḥ saṃtāpayan raṇe pārthaṃ bhūtāny antarhitāni ca
english: Then the great-minded Droṇa brought forth the Brāhma weapon, scorching in the battle both Pārtha and the unseen beings.

sanskrit: tataś cacāla pṛthivī saparvatavanadrumā vavau ca viṣamo vāyuḥ sāgarāś cāpi cukṣubhuḥ
english: Then the earth trembled with its mountains, forests, and trees; a turbulent wind blew, and the oceans too were stirred to their depths.

sanskrit: tatas trāso mahān āsīt kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ sarveṣāṃ caiva bhūtānām udyate 'stre mahātmanā
english: Then great terror seized the armies of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, and indeed all beings, when that weapon was raised by the great-souled one.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho 'py asaṃbhrāntas tad astraṃ pratijaghnivān brahmāstreṇaiva rājendra tataḥ sarvam aśīśamat
english: Then Pārtha too, unshaken, quelled that weapon with the Brahmā weapon itself, O lord of kings, and so brought all to calm.

sanskrit: yadā na gamyate pāraṃ tayor anyatarasya vā tataḥ saṃkulayuddhena tad yuddhaṃ vyakulīkṛtam
english: When neither of the two could be brought to the end of the other, then by a confused melee that combat was thrown into disorder.

sanskrit: nājñāyata tataḥ kiṃ cit punar eva viśāṃ pate pravṛtte tumule yuddhe droṇapāṇḍavayor mṛdhe
english: Thereafter nothing whatever could be made out, O lord of the people, once the tumultuous fray of Droṇa and the Pāṇḍava was joined upon the field.

sanskrit: śarajālaiḥ samākīrṇe meghajālair ivāmbare na sma saṃpatate kaś cid antarikṣacaras tadā
english: With the sky overspread by nets of arrows as by masses of cloud, not a single creature that moves through the air could fly there then.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne narāśvagajasaṃkṣaye duḥśāsano mahārāja dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayat
english: Saṃjaya said: While that slaughter of men, horses, and elephants was thus going on, Duḥśāsana, O great king, did battle with Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

sanskrit: sa tu rukmarathāsakto duḥśāsanaśarārditaḥ amarṣāt tava putrasya śarair vāhān avākirat
english: He, mounted on his golden car and sore wounded by Duḥśāsana's arrows, in his wrath covered the horses of your son with his shafts.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena sa rathas tasya sadhvajaḥ sahasārathiḥ nādṛśyata mahārāja pārṣatasya śaraiś citaḥ
english: In an instant that chariot of his, with its banner and its charioteer, was no longer to be seen, O great king, so thickly was it studded with the arrows of Pārṣata.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu rājendra pāñcālyasya mahātmanaḥ nāśakat pramukhe sthātuṃ śarajālaprapīḍitaḥ
english: But Duḥśāsana, O lord of kings, harried by the nets of arrows, could not stand before the great-souled prince of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: sa tu duḥśāsanaṃ bāṇair vimukhīkṛtya pārṣataḥ kirañ śarasahasrāṇi droṇam evābhyayād raṇe
english: And Pārṣata, having turned Duḥśāsana away with his arrows, scattering thousands of shafts, advanced upon Droṇa himself in the battle.

sanskrit: pratyapadyata hārdikyaḥ kṛtavarmā tadantaram sodaryāṇāṃ trayaś caiva ta enaṃ paryavārayan
english: The son of Hṛdika, Kṛtavarman, moved into the breach, and three brothers as well, and they hemmed him in on every side.

sanskrit: taṃ yamau pṛṣṭhato 'nvaitāṃ rakṣantau puruṣarṣabhau droṇāyābhimukhaṃ yāntaṃ dīpyamānam ivānalam
english: The twins, those bulls among men, followed close behind to guard him as he bore down on Droṇa, blazing like fire.

sanskrit: saṃprahāram akurvaṃs te sarve sapta mahārathāḥ amarṣitāḥ sattvavantaḥ kṛtvā maraṇam agrataḥ
english: All those seven great chariot-warriors joined battle, wrathful and resolute, having set death itself before them.

sanskrit: śuddhātmānaḥ śuddhavṛttā rājan svargapuraskṛtāḥ āryaṃ yuddham akurvanta parasparajigīṣavaḥ
english: Pure of soul and pure of conduct, O king, with heaven held before them, they waged a noble fight, each longing to conquer the other.

sanskrit: śuklābhijanakarmāṇo matimanto janādhipāḥ dharmayuddham ayudhyanta prekṣanto gatim uttamām
english: Of stainless birth and stainless deeds, those wise lords of men fought a righteous fight, with eyes fixed upon the highest goal.

sanskrit: na tatrāsīd adharmiṣṭham aśastraṃ yuddham eva ca nātra karṇī na nālīko na lipto na ca vastakaḥ
english: There was nothing unrighteous in that combat, no fighting without proper weapons; no barbed arrow was there, no hollow reed-shaft, no poisoned dart, nor any double-headed one.

sanskrit: na sūcī kapiśo nātra na gavāsthir gajāsthikaḥ iṣur āsīn na saṃśliṣṭo na pūtir na ca jihmagaḥ
english: No needle-pointed shaft was there, no brown one, none tipped with the bone of ox or elephant; no arrow was barbed, none foul, and none that flew crooked.

sanskrit: ṛjūny eva viśuddhāni sarve śastrāṇy adhārayan suyuddhena parāṃl lokān īpsantaḥ kīrtim eva ca
english: Straight and pure alone were all the weapons they bore, as they sought through fair fighting the higher worlds and renown besides.

sanskrit: tadāsīt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ sarvadoṣavivarjitam caturṇāṃ tava yodhānāṃ tais tribhiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha
english: Then there was a tumultuous combat, free of every fault, between four of your warriors and those three of the Pāṇḍava side.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu tān hitvā tava rājan ratharṣabhān yamābhyāṃ vāritān dṛṣṭvā śīghrāstro droṇam abhyayāt
english: But Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O king, leaving those bulls among your chariot-warriors—seeing them held off by the twins—and swift with his weapons, advanced upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: nivāritās tu te vīrās tayoḥ puruṣasiṃhayoḥ samasajjanta catvāro vātāḥ parvatayor iva
english: Held back by those two lions among men, the four heroes closed together with them, like winds dashing between two mountains.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ yamau sārdhaṃ rathābhyāṃ rathapuṃgavau samāsaktau tato droṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno 'bhyavartata
english: The twins, those foremost of chariot-warriors, each engaged two cars; and meanwhile Dhṛṣṭadyumna bore down upon Droṇa.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā droṇāya pāñcālyaṃ vrajantaṃ yuddhadurmadam yamābhyāṃ tāṃś ca saṃsaktāṃs tadantaram upādravat
english: Seeing the Pāñcāla, battle-frenzied, advancing upon Droṇa, and those others locked in combat with the twins, Duryodhana rushed into the gap.

sanskrit: duryodhano mahārāja kirañ śoṇitabhojanān taṃ sātyakiḥ śīghrataraṃ punar evābhyavartata
english: Duryodhana, O great king, scattering arrows that drink blood; but Sātyaki, swifter still, turned again to meet him.

sanskrit: tau parasparam āsādya samīpe kurumādhavau hasamānau nṛśārdūlāv abhītau samagacchatām
english: Drawing near to each other, those two—the Kuru and the Mādhava, tigers among men—came together fearless and laughing.

sanskrit: bālye vṛttāni sarvāṇi prīyamāṇau vicintya tau anyonyaṃ prekṣamāṇau ca hasamānau punaḥ punaḥ
english: Recalling with fondness all that had passed between them in their boyhood, they gazed upon one another and laughed again and again.

sanskrit: atha duryodhano rājā sātyakiṃ pratyabhāṣata priyaṃ sakhāyaṃ satataṃ garhayan vṛttam ātmanaḥ
english: Then King Duryodhana spoke in answer to Sātyaki, his ever-dear friend, reproaching his own conduct:

sanskrit: dhik krodhaṃ dhik sakhe lobhaṃ dhiṅ mohaṃ dhig amarṣitam dhig astu kṣātram ācāraṃ dhig astu balam aurasam
english: "A curse upon anger, O friend, a curse upon greed, a curse upon delusion, a curse upon wrath! A curse upon the way of the warrior, and a curse upon brute strength of the breast!"

sanskrit: yat tvaṃ mām abhisaṃdhatse tvāṃ cāhaṃ śinipuṃgava tvaṃ hi prāṇaiḥ priyataro mamāhaṃ ca sadā tava
english: "—that you should take aim at me, and I at you, O bull of the Śini race! For you are dearer to me than my own life, and I have ever been so to you."

sanskrit: smarāmi tāni sarvāṇi bālye vṛttāni yāni nau tāni sarvāṇi jīrṇāni sāṃprataṃ nau raṇājire kim anyat krodhalobhābhyāṃ yudhyāmi tvādya sātvata
english: "I remember all those things that passed between us in our boyhood; but now upon the field of battle all of it is undone. What else but through anger and greed do I fight you this day, O Sātvata?"

sanskrit: taṃ tathāvādinaṃ rājan sātyakiḥ pratyabhāṣata prahasan viśikhāṃs tīkṣṇān udyamya paramāstravit
english: To him who spoke thus, O king, Sātyaki, master of the highest weapons, made answer with a laugh, raising aloft his sharp shafts:

sanskrit: neyaṃ sabhā rājaputra na cācāryaniveśanam yatra krīḍitam asmābhis tadā rājan samāgataiḥ
english: "This is no assembly hall, O prince, nor the teacher's dwelling, where once, O king, we sported together when we met."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca kva sā krīḍā gatāsmākaṃ bālye vai śinipuṃgava kva ca yuddham idaṃ bhūyaḥ kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "Whither has that play of our boyhood gone, O bull of the Śini race, and whence again has this battle come? For time is hard to overpass."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu no vidyate kṛtyaṃ dhanena dhanalipsayā yatra yudhyāmahe sarve dhanalobhāt samāgatāḥ
english: "What need have we of wealth, or of the craving for wealth, that here we all do battle, gathered together out of greed for riches?"

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ tathāvādinaṃ tatra rājānaṃ mādhavo 'bravīt evaṃvṛttaṃ sadā kṣatraṃ yad dhantīha gurūn api
english: Saṃjaya said: To the king who spoke thus the Mādhava replied: "Such has ever been the way of the warrior, that here he slays even his elders."

sanskrit: yadi te 'haṃ priyo rājañ jahi māṃ mā ciraṃ kṛthāḥ tvatkṛte sukṛtāṃl lokān gaccheyaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: "If I am dear to you, O king, then slay me, and do not delay; through you may I go to the worlds won by good deeds, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: yā te śaktir balaṃ caiva tat kṣipraṃ mayi darśaya necchāmy etad ahaṃ draṣṭuṃ mitrāṇāṃ vyasanaṃ mahat
english: "What power and strength are yours, show them quickly upon me; I do not wish to behold this—the great calamity that befalls one's friends."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ vyaktam ābhāṣya pratibhāṣya ca sātyakiḥ abhyayāt tūrṇam avyagro nirapekṣo viśāṃ pate
english: Having spoken plainly thus and made his reply, Sātyaki advanced swiftly, unperturbed and heedless of all, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tam āyāntam abhiprekṣya pratyagṛhṇāt tavātmajaḥ śaraiś cāvākirad rājañ śaineyaṃ tanayas tava
english: Beholding him as he came on, your son met him, and your son covered Śaineya with arrows, O king.
